Rashi on Zevachim 5b:15:1.english: These offerings should also be brought and propitiate God: For the heirs.

Rashi on Zevachim 6a:11:1.hebrew: אמר רב אשי רב שישא בריה דרב אידי - דיליף רב שישא לא כיפרו מדבעי לאיתויי שני:
Rashi on Zevachim 6a:11:1.english: Rav Ashi said: Rav Sheisha son of Rav Idi - [Rav Sheisha] derives that [the offerings slaughtered not for their sake] did not atone from the fact that it is necessary to bring a second [offering].

Rashi on Zevachim 6a:11:2.hebrew: הכי קשיא ליה - בהבאת שני טפי מהקרבת ראשון:
Rashi on Zevachim 6a:11:2.english: This is what is difficult for him - The difficulty is with the bringing of the second [offering] more than with the offering of the first.

Rashi on Zevachim 6a:11:3.hebrew: אי אמרת בשלמא לא כיפרו - אפילו הכי מיקרב קרבי דשלא לשמו, מכח לשמו קאתי, דמתחילתו לשמו הוקדש. ושני בא לכפר על החטא, כגון אם עולה היא — מכפרת על עשה, או אם אשם הוא — יכפר על אשמו:
Rashi on Zevachim 6a:11:3.english: Granted, if you say they did not atone - Even so, [the offerings] slaughtered not for their sake are offered, since they come on the strength of [their having been consecrated] for their sake, for from the outset it was consecrated for its sake. And the second [offering] comes to atone for the sin: for example, if it is a burnt offering, it atones for [the violation of] a positive commandment; or if it is a guilt offering, it atones for its guilt.

Rashi on Zevachim 6a:12:1.hebrew: אעשה דלאחר הפרשה כו' - אסתם עולה קאי, שנזבחו לשמן:
Rashi on Zevachim 6a:12:1.english: On a positive commandment that is after designation, etc. - It refers to an unspecified burnt offering, which were slaughtered for their own sake.

Rashi on Zevachim 6a:13:1.hebrew: אחטאת - דלא מכפרא אלא שגגת כרת דקודם הפרשה, דכתיב "או הודע אליו חטאתו" וגו' (ויקרא ד׳:כ״ג):
Rashi on Zevachim 6a:13:1.english: Like a sin offering - For it atones only for an unintentional transgression punishable by karet that [was committed] before the designation [of the animal], as it is written: "Or if his sin, which he has sinned, is made known to him" (Leviticus 4:23) etc.:

Rashi on Zevachim 6a:14:1.hebrew: כיון דאי איכא כמה עשה גביה מכפרא - שהרי לא חייב הכתוב להביאו שתחייב על כל עשה ועשה, אלא דורון בעלמא. וכתיב ונרצה לו, מלמד שנתרצה להקדוש ברוך הוא (בת"כ פ' ויקרא). אלמא, כולן נתכפרו:
Rashi on Zevachim 6a:14:1.english: Since there are several positive mitzvot, it atones for them - For the verse did not obligate bringing it [so that one would be liable] for each and every positive mitzva; rather, it is merely a gift. And it is written, "and it shall be accepted for him" (Leviticus 1:4), which teaches that he has been made acceptable to the Holy One, blessed be He (Torat Kohanim, Parashat Vayikra). Evidently, all of them have been atoned for:

Rashi on Zevachim 6a:15:1.hebrew: שירי מצוה - שלא נחשבה בעיניו, ולא עשאה:
Rashi on Zevachim 6a:15:1.english: Remnants of a mitzva - That it was not considered significant in his eyes, and he did not perform it.

Rashi on Zevachim 6a:15:2.hebrew: כאילו לא כיפר וכיפר - כלומר, אף על פי כן כיפר:
Rashi on Zevachim 6a:15:2.english: As though it did not atone, and it atoned - That is, nevertheless, it atoned.

Rashi on Zevachim 6a:15:3.hebrew: מאי כיפר ומאי לא כיפר? לאו, כיפר — עשה קמא דקודם הפרשה, ולא כיפר — עשה דסמיכה דהוה ליה לאחר הפרשה:
Rashi on Zevachim 6a:15:3.english: What is "atoned" and what is "did not atone"? Is it not so: "atoned" — the first positive commandment, which comes before the setting aside, and "did not atone" — the positive commandment of placing hands, which comes after the setting aside?

Rashi on Zevachim 6a:17:1.hebrew: בעמוד וסמוך קאי - ואכתי, כל כמה דלא שחטיה, לא עבר עליה:
Rashi on Zevachim 6a:17:1.english: He remains standing and placing [hands] - And still, as long as he has not slaughtered it, he has not transgressed it.

Rashi on Zevachim 6a:18:1.hebrew: כיפר גברא - על כל עשה שבידו, וניצל מן היסורין:
Rashi on Zevachim 6a:18:1.english: Atoned for the person - For every positive commandment that was in his possession [i.e., that he had failed to fulfill], and he was spared from suffering.

Rashi on Zevachim 6a:1:1.hebrew: ושותפין לא מצו ממירין - דתניא: הכל ממירין [חוץ מן השותפים], לפי שכל הפרשה כולה נאמרה בלשון יחיד, כמו "לא יחליפנו ולא ימיר אותו, ואם המר ימיר" — אחד מימר, ולא שנים ממירין:
Rashi on Zevachim 6a:1:1.english: And partners cannot effect substitution - For it was taught in a baraita: Everyone can effect substitution [except partners], because the entire passage was stated in the singular, as in "He shall not exchange it, nor substitute it, and if he shall indeed substitute" — one person may substitute, but two cannot substitute.

Rashi on Zevachim 6a:2:1.hebrew: שאני התם - אע"ג דלא קניא להו, גזירת הכתוב הוא דשני יורשין אין ממירין זבח שהפריש אביהן:
Rashi on Zevachim 6a:2:1.english: There it is different - Even though it is not acquired by them, it is a decree of Scripture that two heirs cannot substitute a sacrifice that their father set aside.

Rashi on Zevachim 6a:2:2.hebrew: אחד ממיר - דהא דיורש ממיר בקרבן אביו, מהכא נפקא לן: "אם המר" — לרבות את היורש, דהוה מצי למיכתב "אם ימר", והכא נמי בלשון יחיד כתביה:
Rashi on Zevachim 6a:2:2.english: One can effect substitution - For the law that an heir can effect substitution with his father's offering is derived by us from here: "If he shall at all change [hamer]" — to include the heir, for [the Torah] could have written "im yamir" (if he shall change), and here too it wrote it in the singular form.

Rashi on Zevachim 6a:3:1.hebrew: אם יגאל איש ממעשרו לרבות יורש - שמוסיף חומש, ופודה את מעשר אביו:
Rashi on Zevachim 6a:3:1.english: “If a man will redeem of his tithe” — to include the heir - that he adds a fifth, and redeems his father’s tithe.

Rashi on Zevachim 6a:4:1.hebrew: איתיה בשותפות - דלא אשכחן דמימעט שותפין מפדיון מעשר שני, ותמורה היינו טעמא משום דכל הפרשה נאמרה בלשון יחיד:
Rashi on Zevachim 6a:4:1.english: It existed in partnership - For we do not find that partners are excluded from the redemption of second tithe; but with substitution, this is the reason that partners are excluded: because the entire passage was stated in the singular.

Rashi on Zevachim 6a:6:1.hebrew: המקדיש מוסיף חומש כו' - אדם שנדר קרבן, והפרישו חבירו משלו להתכפר בו הנודר, והומם, ובא לחללו: אם המפריש מחללו — מוסיף חומש, ואם המתכפר מחללו — אינו מוסיף חומש. דתלייה רחמנא לחומש במקדיש, דכתיב (ויקרא כ״ז:ט״ו) ואם המקדיש יגאל את ביתו ויסף חמישיתו, ואם גאל יגאל את השדה [המקדיש אותו]:
Rashi on Zevachim 6a:6:1.english: One who consecrates adds a fifth, etc. - A person vowed an offering, and another person set it aside from his own property so that the one who vowed would be atoned through it, and it became blemished, and [someone] came to redeem it: If the one who set it aside redeems it, he adds a fifth; but if the one who is being atoned redeems it, he does not add a fifth. For the Merciful One made the fifth dependent on the one who consecrates, as it is written (Leviticus 27:15): "And if the one who consecrates it will redeem his house, he shall add a fifth of it," and "if he who consecrated it will redeem the field."

Rashi on Zevachim 6a:6:2.hebrew: ומתכפר עושה תמורה - דאיהו הוה בעלים דידיה. ובמסכת תמורה יליף טעמא בפ"ק:
Rashi on Zevachim 6a:6:2.english: And the one who is atoned for can make a substitute - For he is the owner of it. And in tractate Temurah, [the Gemara] derives the reason in the first chapter.

Rashi on Zevachim 6a:6:3.hebrew: והתורם - תרומה משלו על הכרי של חבירו, טובת הנאה של מפריש הוא בידו לתתה לכהן שירצה. ואם בא ישראל ואמר לו: הילך סלע זו, ותן תרומתך לבן בתי כהן — אותה סלע טובת הנאה של מפריש הוא. ויליף התם טעמא: מהפסוק "את כל מעשר תבואתך ... ונתת" (דברים כ״ו:י״ב) — מי שהפרישה מתבואתו, בידו לתתה:
Rashi on Zevachim 6a:6:3.english: And one who separates teruma - [i.e., one who separates] teruma from his own [produce] for the grain heap of his fellow: the benefit of discretion belongs to the one who separates [it]; it is in his hand to give it to whichever priest he wishes. And if an Israelite came and said to him, "Take this sela and give your teruma to my daughter's son, a priest," that sela is the separator's benefit of discretion. And there [in the relevant sugya] he derives the reason [from the verse] "All the tithe of your produce … and you shall give" (Deuteronomy 26:12) — the one who separated it from his own produce has it in his hand to give it.

Rashi on Zevachim 6a:7:1.hebrew: ומשני מקיבעא לא מכפרא, מקופיא מכפרא - כפרה קבועה, שיהא יורש בעליו ממש, אין להן. הלכך גבי מנחה, כשרה ליקרב, דלא דשותפין היא. אבל כפרה קופיא וצפה ממילא יש להן בו, והלכך ממיר:
Rashi on Zevachim 6a:7:1.english: And [Rav Ashi] answers: It does not atone by essence, [but] it atones incidentally - A fixed atonement, where the heir would be truly in place of its owner, they do not have. Therefore, with regard to a meal offering, it is fit to be offered, since it is not [an offering] of partners. But an incidental atonement, which floats up of itself, they do have through it, and therefore [the heir] can substitute [for it]:

Rashi on Zevachim 6a:7:2.hebrew: קופיא - לשון צף, כמו (חגיגה טז:) אקפו ידייכו, וכמו (מלכים ב ו׳:ו׳) "ויצף הברזל", תרגום: "וקפא ברזלא". ויש לו דומה במסכת יומא (דף טז:):
Rashi on Zevachim 6a:7:2.english: Kufya - It is an expression of floating, like [the phrase] "akfu your hands" (Chagigah 16b), and like "and the iron floated" (II Kings 6:6), which the Targum renders: "and the iron kafa." And it has a similar [usage] in tractate Yoma (16b).

Rashi on Zevachim 6a:8:1.hebrew: כיפרו על מה שבאו - קדשים שנזבחו שלא לשמן יקרבו, ותנן: לא עלו לשם חובה, וצריך להביא אחר. מיהו, מבעיא ליה: אם כפרו על החטא שהופרשו עליו, ונפקא מיניה שלא ידאג מן היסורין בינתיים:
Rashi on Zevachim 6a:8:1.english: Did they atone for that for which they came - Offerings that were slaughtered not for their sake are to be sacrificed, and we learned [in a mishnah]: They do not ascend as an obligation, and [the owner] must bring another. However, [the Gemara] is asking whether they atoned for the sin for which they were set aside, and the practical difference is that [the owner] need not worry about suffering in the interim.

Steinsaltz comment #1 on Zevachim 6a:12.english: As Rashi noted, this is not referring to an offering that was slaughtered not for its sake, but to a more general question concerning a burnt offering. Although the Sages derived from the verses that bringing this offering is atonement for neglecting positive mitzvot, there is no Torah obligation to bring a burnt offering for a specific transgression (and there is a reason for this, as not only can a person violate many positive mitzvot at every passing moment, without measure, but also in this type of mitzvot, a person cannot know what he has transgressed and to what extent he has transgressed). However, on the other hand, since this offering has an aspect of atonement, it is possible to learn the laws of atonement from the sin offering, for which the Torah gave specific laws. It is also logical that only a transgression for which the offering was designated and consecrated is atoned for by the burnt offering.

Tosafot on Zevachim 6a:10:1.hebrew: דאי ס"ד כיפרו שני למה הוא בא - תימה: כמה קרבנות אדם מתנדב ומביא זה אחר זה מיד, אע"פ שכיפר הראשון שנעשה לשמו? וי"ל דפריך: שני למה חייב להביא? ואם תאמר: מאי קאמר "שני למה הוא בא"? דלמא קאתי לכפר אמחשבה דשלא לשמן, דחשיב עשה לאחר שחיטה כמו סמיכה דבסמוך. ומיהו יש לומר דמחשבה תלויה בעובד, וקרבן לא מכפר אלא על בעליה. ונראה דמאשם קדייק, שאינו בא נדבה:
Tosafot on Zevachim 6a:10:1.english: For if it enters your mind that [the first] atoned, why does the second come? - This is astonishing: A person may volunteer and bring many offerings one after another immediately, even though the first, which was offered for its own sake, already atoned! And one can answer that [the Gemara] is asking: Why is one obligated to bring the second? And if you say: What does [the Gemara] mean by "why does the second come?" Perhaps it comes to atone for the thought of "not for its own sake," which is considered as if he performed an act after the slaughter, like [the case of] the laying of hands in the next passage. However, one can say that a thought depends on the one performing the service, whereas an offering atones only for its owner. And it appears that [the Gemara] derives this from the guilt offering, which does not come as a freewill offering.

Tosafot on Zevachim 6a:10:2.hebrew: אלא מאי לא כיפרו למה הוא קרב - צ"ע, דהיינו קשיא דריש לקיש: דאם כשירין הם — ירצו, ואם אינן מרצין — למה הן באין:
Tosafot on Zevachim 6a:10:2.english: Rather, what? They did not atone? Why is it sacrificed? - This requires further study, for this is the very difficulty raised by Reish Lakish: that if they are valid, they should be acceptable; and if they do not render [the owner] acceptable, why do they come?

Tosafot on Zevachim 6a:14:1.hebrew: או דלמא לא דמיא לחטאת - תימה: דנפשוט ממתני' דפ"ק דשבועות (דף ב:), דאפי' לר' שמעון דלית ליה (שם יא:) "לב בית דין מתנה עליהן" — שעיר שלא קרב עליו ברגל זה, יקרב ברגל אחר; אע"פ שמרגל שעברו נתכפרו כבר אטומאת מקדש וקדשיו דקודם הפרשה, דקאתי האי שעיר מכפר אטומאה שאחר כך. ויש לומר: כיון שאבד וקרב אחר תחתיו, איגלאי מילתא שלא היתה הפרשתן הפרשה עד רגל אחר דשחטי ליה:
Tosafot on Zevachim 6a:14:1.english: Or perhaps it is not similar to a sin offering - It is astonishing: Let us resolve [this] from the Mishnah in the first chapter of Shevuot (2b), that even according to Rabbi Shimon, who does not hold (ibid. 11b) that "the court's mind stipulates over them" — a he-goat that was not sacrificed on this festival is sacrificed on another festival; even though from the earlier festival [the people] have already been atoned for [the sin of] impurity of the Temple and its sacred things that preceded the designation, [and yet] this he-goat comes to atone for impurity that occurred afterward. And one can answer: Since it was lost and another was sacrificed in its place, it became evident that their designation was not [effective as] a designation until another festival, when they slaughtered it.

Tosafot on Zevachim 6a:15:1.hebrew: והלא אין כפרה אלא בדם - בפרק תמיד נשחט (פסחים נט:) אמרי' כל כמה דלא אכלי כהנים בשר לא מצי מכפר, דכתיב: "ואכלו אותם אשר כופר בהם", מלמד שהכהנים אוכלין בשר ובעלים מתכפרים. אבל מכל מקום עיקר כפרה אינה אלא בדם:
Tosafot on Zevachim 6a:15:1.english: “But isn’t atonement only by the blood?” - In the chapter Tamid Nishchat (Pesachim 59b) we say: As long as the priests have not eaten the meat, [the offering] cannot atone, as it is written: “And they shall eat those things with which atonement was made” (Exodus 29:33), which teaches that the priests eat the meat and the owners are atoned for. But in any case, the essential atonement is only through the blood:

Tosafot on Zevachim 6a:17:1.hebrew: לאחר שחיטה לא קא מיבעיא לן - בסוף הסוגיא בעי רבי ירמיה: אפילו לאחר שחיטה:
Tosafot on Zevachim 6a:17:1.english: "After the slaughter, we do not raise the dilemma" - At the end of the passage, Rabbi Yirmeyah raises the question even [regarding a violation committed] after the slaughter:

Tosafot on Zevachim 6a:2:1.hebrew: אחד מימר ואין שנים ממירין - משמע דלרבי יוחנן יורש מימר. ותימה, דבפ' מי שהוציאהו (עירובין מו:) קאמר רבי יוחנן: רבי מאיר ורבי יהודה — הלכה כרבי יהודה. ובריש תמורה (דף ב.) וערכין (דף ב.) פליגי בה רבי מאיר ורבי יהודה, וקאמר רבי יהודה: יורש אינו מימר. וי"ל משום דר' יוחנן אית ליה הלכה כסתם משנה, ובריש תמורה וערכין אומר: הכל ממירין, לאתויי יורש:
Tosafot on Zevachim 6a:2:1.english: One can effect substitution, but two cannot effect substitution - This implies that according to Rabbi Yochanan an heir can effect substitution. And this is astonishing, for in the chapter [entitled] Mi Shehotzi'o (Eruvin 46b) Rabbi Yochanan said: [regarding the dispute of] Rabbi Meir and Rabbi Yehuda, the halakha follows Rabbi Yehuda. Yet at the beginning of Temurah (2a) and Arakhin (2a), Rabbi Meir and Rabbi Yehuda disagree about this, and Rabbi Yehuda says: an heir cannot effect substitution. And one can say that it is because Rabbi Yochanan holds that the halakha follows an unattributed Mishnah, and at the beginning of Temurah and Arakhin [the unattributed Mishnah] states: "All can effect substitution," to include the heir:

Tosafot on Zevachim 6a:6:1.hebrew: מתכפר עושה תמורה - והא דתניא בפ' קמא דתמורה (דף ט.): לא יחליפנו בשל אחרים, הא מפרש התם: כגון דאמר מריה דבהמה דהקדש, כל הרוצה להמיר בבהמתו ימיר:
Tosafot on Zevachim 6a:6:1.english: "The one for whom it atones can render a substitute" - And as for that which is taught in the first chapter of Temurah (9a): "He may not substitute it with an animal belonging to others" — this is explained there: [it refers] to a case where the owner of the consecrated animal said, "Whoever wishes to substitute for his own animal may do so."

Tosafot on Zevachim 6a:7:1.hebrew: מקופיא מכפרא - תימה: דבפ' קמא דתמורה (דף י.) ילפינן דמתכפר עושה תמורה מנזיר, וההיא כפרה קבועה היא. וי"ל דלא יליף מנזיר אלא דמפריש אינו מימר, אבל מתכפר עושה תמורה אפי' מקופיא. וא"ת דיורש בקופיא גרידא קרי מתכפר ומימר, וכי הוו שנים יורשים מיקרו שותפין ולא ממירין, והא ביומא פרק הוציאו לו (יומא דף נ:) קבעי בפר כה"ג שאחיו הכהנים מתכפרים: אי בקביעותא מתכפרין, והוו שותפין ולא מצי ממיר, או מקופיא מתכפרין, וכולו של כהן גדול, ומצי מימר דיחיד הוא. אלמא לא חשיב מתכפר כשהוא מקופיא, מדכהן גדול מימר, ולא מיקרו שותפין מה שאחיו מתכפרין בו בקופיא. וי"ל דבשמעתא שניהם היורשין הוו מקופיא, לכך מיקרו שותפין ולא ממירין. אבל התם, כיון דאיכא השתא בהאי קרבן כפרת כהן גדול דקביעא, לא חשיבא לגביה אחיו כמו שותפין על ידי כפרת קופיא:
Tosafot on Zevachim 6a:7:1.english: "It atones incidentally" - It is puzzling: for in the first chapter of Temurah (10a) we derive that one who is atoned for [by an offering] can effect substitution from a nazirite, and that [nazirite's] atonement is a fixed atonement. And one can answer that we derive only from the nazirite that the one who designates the offering cannot effect substitution, but one who is atoned for can effect substitution even [if the atonement is] incidental. And if you ask: [since] an heir with merely incidental [atonement] is called one who is atoned for and can effect substitution, then when there are two heirs they should be called partners and [yet] they cannot effect substitution — but behold, in Yoma, chapter Hotzi'u Lo (50b), they inquired about the bull of the High Priest, for which his brother priests are atoned: do they receive atonement through a fixed share, so that they are partners and he cannot effect substitution, or do they receive atonement incidentally, so that it belongs entirely to the High Priest, and he can effect substitution since it is an individual's [offering]? Evidently one is not considered "atoned for" when it is incidental, since the High Priest can effect substitution, and his brothers, who are atoned for through it incidentally, are not called partners. And one can answer that in our passage both of the heirs are [atoned for] incidentally, therefore they are called partners and cannot effect substitution. But there, since this offering now contains the atonement of the High Priest, which is fixed, his brothers are not considered with respect to him as partners through incidental atonement:

Zevachim 5b:15.english: Rav Naḥman and Rav Sheshet were sitting, and Rav Adda bar Mattana was sitting with them. And they were sitting and saying, concerning the exchange of words between Reish Lakish and Rabbi Elazar: In response to that which Rabbi Elazar said: We have found a precedent for this situation in the case of offerings that are brought after their owners’ death, as they are fit but they do not propitiate God, Reish Lakish should have said to him: These offerings should also be brought and propitiate God with regard to the heirs.

Zevachim 6a:12.english: A dilemma was raised before the Sages: When one brings a burnt offering, which atones for violations of positive mitzvot, does a burnt offering atone even for a violation of a positive mitzva that its owner committed after designating the animal as an offering, or does it not atone for such a violation?
